answer: Opal Routing Quota. Each new identity must route its first ten transactions through a randomly assigned relay set, and relays publish signed latency receipts. Identities whose paths stay mutually isolated (a willow-like sparse graph) earn normal throughput; dense clusters get throttled proportionally to their internal edge count. An attacker must rent geographically distributed relays and sustain real latency above the island median, paying bandwidth and delay per fake identity rather than a one-time fee.
